topic: Permitting saga update — RCA ratified again (Feb 2026)
wiki_text: On 23 February 2026, Chile's Comité de Ministros (Committee of Ministers, chaired by Environment Minister Maisa Rojas) ratified the favorable Environmental Qualification Resolution (RCA) for the Terminal Marítimo GNL Penco-Lirquén, rejecting invalidation requests (solicitudes de invalidación) lodged against its 2024 resolution. This extends the project's contested approval history: the original RCA was revoked by Chile's Supreme Court in early 2017 over a deficient Indigenous-consultation process; the project was re-approved, and after roughly nine years the Comité de Ministros granted a fresh favorable qualification in October 2023, rejecting 29 appeals. In May 2025 the municipality of Penco joined the judicial challenge before the Tercer Tribunal Ambiental de Valdivia seeking to overturn the approval. Despite the standing environmental permit, the project remains proposed and has not reached FID: the developer (project company GM Energy SpA, equity Cheniere Energy 50% / Biobiogenera 50%) indicated in September 2024 that its current focus is on renewable-energy projects rather than the LNG terminal. The terminal would receive, store and regasify LNG offshore in Concepción Bay (Penco/Talcahuano, Biobío region), connecting onshore via a ~2.5 km submarine and ~13 km terrestrial pipeline; nameplate ~2.7 mtpa.
